quote: Y'all don't do a trailer. You don't do a trailer, do you?
stewart_read: Rep phrases a qualifying question in a confusing double-negative that momentarily muddies the roof/home-type verification; customer answers cooperatively despite the awkward phrasing.
coaching_implication: Clean up phrasing on manufactured-home qualifier — ask directly ('Is it a manufactured/mobile home or a standard house?') to avoid confusion on a hard-gate question.

stewart_read: Fifteen years sits exactly on the schema's roof-age DQ boundary (roof_age_over_15_no_replacement_planned), yet the rep says 'not too bad' and moves on without probing roof condition or replacement plans.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep didn't recognize this as a live DQ boundary and simply reassured the customer. Strategic read is not supported — there's no evidence the rep intentionally deferred this to a closer.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to treat 15-year roofs as a flag requiring a follow-up question (condition, any leaks, replacement plans) rather than a quick reassurance — this is a second live disqualifier sitting unresolved in the same call as the credit stall.

quote: The main requirements for solar are just that you own your home and have a credit score above 650.
stewart_read: Rep states 650 as the threshold, matching the drift already flagged in another call (SESSION18_fcbf33c1) against the schema's documented 670 — indicates this may be a floor-wide script inconsistency rather than one rep's error.
coaching_implication: Flag for Kenny: confirm whether 650 or 670 is the live threshold; if reps are drifting inconsistently, standardize the number in training.

quote: Not right at the moment. I don't think it's 650, though.
stewart_read: This is not Lawanda's own credit — it's her guess about Neil's, the actual lead. The rep takes a proxy's unverified guess about a third party's credit and treats it as effectively disqualifying, per qualifiers.credit_qualifier's open policy question (stated vs. pulled credit). The uncertainty here is compounded: even 'stated' credit policy assumes the person stating it is the one whose credit it is.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: the rep may be following a 'never push past a self-disqualifying answer' norm. But there's no evidence the rep recognized the guess was secondhand — the rep never asks 'is that your understanding of his score, or has he checked recently?'
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to distinguish a firsthand stated score from a secondhand guess. When the person on the phone isn't the lead, the rep should get the actual lead's confirmation (call Neil, or ask Lawanda to have Neil check) before treating an uncertain proxy guess as a stopping point.

quote: Feel free to call this number back, though.
stewart_read: Call ends with no owned next step — no callback scheduled, no follow-up text, no verification path for Neil's actual credit. This is a passive close, not a booked callback.
coaching_implication: Even on a stalled qualifier, the rep should own a next step: 'I'll check back with you in two weeks' or 'have Neil check his score and I'll call Thursday' rather than leaving it to the customer to reinitiate.

quote: And then if it's not 650, once it gets to that point, we'd be more than happy to run a quote for you.
stewart_read: Reinforces the same soft, undated close — a vague future contingency rather than any concrete follow-up mechanism.
coaching_implication: Same coaching note as above: replace vague contingency language with a concrete owned action (specific callback date, or a text/link to check credit).
